passage: I live next door and the walls are thin, so I heard all of it. Samir yelled, "That's MY sketchbook! You scribbled on my dragon page!" His younger brother Francis stood there holding a red crayon, lip trembling. Samir's face was red and his fists were tight, but he did not hit him. He snatched the sketchbook and stomped off. Later, through the balcony, I heard him say, "Next time ask me first. Mummy, can we make a rule about this?" Their mother agreed. Samir put the sketchbook on the high shelf. I can't be sure how he felt inside, but he sounded upset more than mean.

qa.q: What was Francis holding when Samir yelled?
qa.a: He was holding a red crayon.

qa.q: What do Samir's red face and tight fists suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: They suggest he was very angry, but the neighbour thinks he sounded more upset than mean, since he did not hit Francis.

qa.q: What did Samir do afterwards that worked better than hitting?
qa.a: He asked Francis to ask first, asked Mummy for a rule, and put the sketchbook on the high shelf.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt when Samir shouted?
qa.a: Francis was probably scared and sorry, since his lip trembled as he stood holding the crayon.

grounding: A neighbour observes an older brother's fair anger over a sketchbook, handled with words and a rule.

passage:
Leila found her sketchbook on the living-room floor of their Toronto apartment. Her little brother Ivan had drawn purple robots all over the fox she'd spent a week on.
"IVAN! That's MINE!" she shouted. Ivan's eyes went wide. For a second she wanted to grab his toy truck and snap it.
She didn't. She stomped to her room and counted to twenty.
Then she came back. "Ivan, that fox took me a week. You can't use my sketchbook without asking."
Ivan's lip wobbled. "I wanted to draw like you."
That evening Leila asked Mom for a rule: nobody touches her sketchbook. Mom agreed and gave Leila a drawer with a small lock. Leila gave Ivan some plain paper.

qa.q: What had Ivan drawn over Leila's fox?
What was Leila feeling when she saw the fox?
qa.a: She was furious, wanting to shout and even break Ivan's toy truck.

qa.q: What did Leila do instead of breaking Ivan's truck?
qa.a: She calmed down, explained to Ivan what he did wrong, asked Mom for a rule and got a locked drawer for her sketchbook.

qa.q: How might Ivan have felt when Leila shouted?
qa.a: Ivan was startled and upset, since he had only wanted to draw like his sister.

grounding: A girl shouts when her younger brother uses her sketchbook; her anger is fair, and she then tells him calmly, asks a parent for a rule and locks it away.

passage:
The clinic waiting room was stuffy and the wait for Nani's check-up was long. Abhinav had brought his sketchbook to pass the time, but he'd gone for water. When he came back, his little brother Yash had scribbled over his best cricket drawing.
"Yash! That's mine!" His voice was loud enough that the receptionist looked up. His fist clenched. He wanted to snatch Yash's toy car and throw it.
Abhinav took a deep breath. "Yash, don't use my book without asking."
Then he turned to Mummy. "Can we make a rule? My sketchbook is only mine."
Mummy nodded. "Agreed. Yash, ask first." Abhinav tucked the book into his bag and zipped it shut.

qa.a: In the clinic waiting room, for Nani's check-up.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel when he saw his drawing scribbled on?
qa.a: He was angry, with a clenched fist and the urge to throw Yash's toy car.

qa.q: What did Abhinav do that was wise?
qa.a: He told Yash calmly, asked Mummy to set a rule, and zipped his sketchbook away.

qa.q: How might Mummy see Abhinav's request for a rule?
qa.a: Mummy sees it as fair, agreeing straight away and telling Yash to ask first.

grounding: A boy shouts when his younger brother scribbles in his sketchbook in a clinic waiting room, then tells him calmly, asks his mother for a rule and puts the book away.
